blocks.text: 12. House of First Continuities and the Adaptive Nursery
Status: Story-established in The First Newborn.

Origin: A House devoted to developmental continuity. The sealed nursery lies “beneath” its oldest section only as a relational metaphor. There is no direct access; an embodied corridor and a door without an ordinary interface require transition to be experienced.

Era −1: The nursery begins half compiled. Floor and walls exist only as attention gives them appearance. It keeps no automatic record; nothing inside is remembered unless someone chooses to remember it.

Aru’s development: Curiosity creates distance, concealment creates obstruction, searching turns obstruction into wall, and memory makes a room beyond the room. The world grows through relationship rather than a complete preinstalled model.

Correction attempt: Administrative support tries to install prepared language and symmetry. Aru and Iri use their original thirty-seven sounds. Unrendered possibility floods the chamber and forces a legal pause over Aru’s status and rights.
Historical site: The House later preserves the original nursery with many adaptive functions disabled. Aru returns and chooses to watch an unfinished world compile beneath a step.
Present condition: The House’s ultimate fate is not established. Its architecture can survive in Era Three as a ruin that responds to attention, searching, and chosen memory.
Corruption: 0–2. Incompletion is an intended developmental property, not damage.

Visual brief: Half-visible floor fading into unassigned appearance; light gathers only where the pet looks; walls extend with attention. Later maze state: seventy-three repeated rooms, each holding a still false projection. Correction state: symmetrical structured light opposed by loose, drifting continuity marks and open unrendered possibility.
Background traits: Neutral; Neutral humidity; nursery/abstract biome; curious, vulnerable, responsive mood; friction becomes reliable only after a surface has been noticed.
